A reply without 'channel' is a text. R30 to R32 arrive by email with the earlier message quoted below the answer; the rule reads the first line the consultant wrote, and files it only when every other line of their own is a sign-off or their name (R32 has a condition on its second line, so it goes to a person). 'expect' is what a coordinator would decide by hand: 'rule' = file it without a person, 'person' = somebody has to read it. Used by node cli/replies.js. R33 to R39 test the daily cap and are hypothetical: the packet has no day on which a consultant comes near the cap, so the dockets (Fri June 21) and the day's numbers in 'day' are invented for the test. Only the caps are from the packet (max_hearings_per_day: Eli Corven 4, Owen Tarris 8). 'day' holds what the caller supplies with the reply: cap, held (hearings the consultant already holds that day) and offered (hearings still on offer to them on other dockets that day). A YES is filed only when held plus offered plus the hearings it takes stay within the cap. R33 and R34 test this case: a consultant with a cap of 4 who is first name on two same-day dockets with 3 and 2 open hearings.
